title: [CI] Required PR check compiles the NUnit suite but runs none of its ~2,990 test cases
body:
## Summary
The required `ci` job depends on lint, tls-interop and h2-interop only. lint compiles Tests/ in the shadow build without running them, and h2-interop runs 15 HTTP/2 scenarios plus a few buffered rows. A regression in the HTTP/1.1 parser, cookie jar, redirect handling or WebSocket close path therefore merges green and is found only at the next periodic host-editor run.

## Location
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:148`

## Problem
ci.yml:148-157: the required `ci` job needs only lint, tls-interop and h2-interop. lint runs check.sh --full, whose shadow build compiles Tests/ with analyzers off (Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:306-308) and never runs a test. h2-interop runs the 15 scenarios of Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Adversarial plus buffered GET/POST rows on .NET 8. fuzz.yml is path-filtered and not in `needs`; soak.yml and autobahn.yml are workflow_dispatch only. Tests/ holds 2,987 [Test]/[TestCase]/[UnityTest] attributes; 324 of the 365 Tests/Runtime .cs files reference neither UnityEngine nor [UnityTest] (about 2,700 attributes). Tools~/h2-interop/TurboHTTP.H2Interop.csproj:34-35 already compiles Tests/Runtime sources into a plain .NET harness and Tools~/soak runs UHttpClient outside Unity, so the technique exists. Static-file fixtures such as Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs (asmdef JSON) also only run in the host editor.

**Failure scenario.** A PR changes Http11ResponseParser chunk handling, CookieJar domain matching, RedirectInterceptor credential stripping or WebSocket close handling and breaks an existing test. lint, tls-interop and h2-interop stay green (none of them touches those paths), the waves merger merges on green `ci`, and the break is found only at the next periodic host-editor run, mixed with every other PR merged since.

## Suggested fix
Add a `unit` job that builds a plain .NET NUnit harness from the engine-free test folders (Transport parsers/HPACK/HTTP2 connection, WebSocket framing, JSON, Middleware, Cache, Retry, Auth, Files on MockTransport) against the shadow DLLs, the way h2-interop links Adversarial/*.cs, and add it to `needs` of `ci`. Start with the pure parser/codec fixtures; move asmdef/link.xml text invariants from Tests/Editor into check_repo.py.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `unit` CI job builds a plain .NET NUnit harness from the engine-free test folders (Transport parsers, HPACK, HTTP/2 connection, WebSocket framing, JSON, Middleware, Cache, Retry, Auth, Files on MockTransport) against the shadow DLLs and runs it.
- [ ] The `unit` job is listed in `needs` of the required `ci` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
- [ ] A deliberately broken parser or cookie-jar assertion makes the PR check fail (demonstrated once in the PR description); the harness covers at least the pure parser/codec fixtures under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ at first.
- [ ] Asmdef/link.xml text invariants in Tests/Editor are moved into Tools~/ci/check_repo.py or documented as host-editor only.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. .github/workflows/ci.yml:148-157: `ci` needs only lint, tls-interop, h2-interop. lint runs check.sh --full; the shadow build only compiles Tests/ (Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:306-308, RunAnalyzers=false) and runs no NUnit test. fuzz.yml is path-filtered and not in `needs`; soak.yml and autobahn.yml are workflow_dispatch only. My count: 2,970 [Test]/[TestCase]/[UnityTest] attributes under Tests/; 324 Tests/Runtime .cs files reference neither UnityEngine nor [UnityTest]. Tools~/h2-interop/TurboHTTP.H2Interop.csproj:34-35 does link Tests/Runtime sources into a plain .NET harness, so the proposed technique exists. Not refuted, but it is a documented owner decision, not an oversight: ci.yml:145-146 and testing.md 'Host-editor gates' (no UNITY_LICENSE, #188 closed) make the periodic host-editor run after every waves run the Unity gate, so a regression is found post-merge rather than never. testing.md also warns a green .NET harness proves logic only (Mono differences). No open issue tracks a plain-.NET unit job. Lowered to medium: process/coverage gap with a documented post-merge mitigation, not a product defect.

Related: #404.

title: [CI] Fuzz PR trigger ignores Core/Internal and Transport/Internal code the parsers call, and the fuzz workflow is not required
body:
## Summary
fuzz.yml triggers only on Tools~/fuzz, Http1, Http2, WebSocket and JSON paths, although the fuzzed parsers depend on SegmentedBuffer, ByteArrayPool, HttpHeaders and Transport/Internal helpers. The fuzz job is also not in `needs` of `ci`, so a failing run does not block merge. A change to SegmentedBuffer or EncodingHelper that breaks parser bounds handling gets its first fuzz signal after merge.

## Location
- `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml:10`

## Problem
fuzz.yml:10-16 triggers on Tools~/fuzz, Runtime/Transport/Http1, Http2, Runtime/WebSocket and Runtime/JSON only. The parsers depend on Runtime/Core/Internal (SegmentedBuffer, ByteArrayPool: Http11ResponseParser.cs uses both; WebSocketFrameReader and MessageAssembler rent from ByteArrayPool), Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders and Runtime/Transport/Internal (EncodingHelper.IsRfc9110TChar and Latin1 in Http11ResponseParser.cs and HpackDecoder.cs, HttpFieldValidator, TrailerFieldValidator); run.sh instruments TurboHTTP.Core for that reason (:63-64). ci.yml:150 does not list the fuzz job, so a failing fuzz run does not block the merge.

**Failure scenario.** A PR changes SegmentedBuffer.GetWriteSpan or EncodingHelper's tchar table and breaks bounds handling in the HTTP/1.1 parser. No fuzz job starts for the PR; the first signal is the next Monday run, after the merge.

## Suggested fix
Add Runtime/Core/Internal/**, Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders*.cs and Runtime/Transport/Internal/** to the paths, and run a short always-on corpus replay (`Tools~/fuzz/run.sh` default driver, seconds) inside the required lint or unit job so the committed seeds and regression inputs gate every PR.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] fuzz.yml path filters include Runtime/Core/Internal/**, Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders*.cs and Runtime/Transport/Internal/**.
- [ ] A short corpus replay of the committed seeds and regression inputs (`Tools~/fuzz/run.sh` default driver) runs inside the required lint or unit job on every PR.
- [ ] A seed that crashes a parser makes the required check fail (demonstrated in the PR).

title: [Testing] Phase 19 allocation baselines are round power-of-two ceilings from a single February run, so the 10% gate cannot detect regressions
body:
## Summary
phase19-allocation-baselines.json holds 32768, 49152, 2048 and 8192 bytes per operation, captured once on 2026-02-21, and Phase19AllocationGateTests allows baseline x 1.10. These values are not measured numbers, so a real regression of several KB per request stays under the ceiling. CLAUDE.md requires hot paths to stay allocation-free where they already are.

## Location
- `Tests/Benchmarks/phase19-allocation-baselines.json:8`

## Problem
phase19-allocation-baselines.json: capturedAtUtc 2026-02-21, maxBytesPerOperation 32768, 49152, 2048, 8192 for the four scenarios; git log shows one commit for the file. Phase19AllocationGateTests.cs:84-93 allows baseline * 1.10. The record mode writes observed numbers (:60-67), which would not be exact powers of two. BenchmarkTests.cs:20 uses the same 32768 bytes per mock request and calls it a `trend guardrail`. No journal entry records the observed bytes/op (rg `bytes/op=` in Development~/docs: none). The test also skips outside the Editor (:33-36).

**Failure scenario.** A change adds a 4 KB allocation to every warm request through the pipeline (for example a per-request header list). If the real figure is a few KB, the result stays under 36 KB and AllocationScenarios_RespectBaselineBudget passes; the regression is not reported although CLAUDE.md requires hot paths to stay allocation-free where they already are.

## Suggested fix
Run the gate in record mode on the reference editor, commit the observed values with a small margin (as the streaming gates do with AllocationBudget per profile), and re-record when a deliberate change moves them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The gate is run in record mode on the reference editor and the observed bytes/op are committed with a small margin per scenario (no round ceilings).
- [ ] A test change that adds a 4 KB per-request allocation makes AllocationScenarios_RespectBaselineBudget fail (verified locally and noted in the PR).
- [ ] The re-record procedure is documented next to the baseline file or in testing.md.

title: [Testing] AssertAsync.ThrowsAsync documents exact exception type but matches derived types, so negative tests pass on the wrong failure
body:
## Summary
AssertAsync.Expect<T> uses `catch (T expected)`, which accepts subclasses, while its XML doc and testing.md say the exact type is matched. TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync behaves the same. Tests such as `ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>` therefore also pass on ObjectDisposedException, WebSocketException passes for UHttpException, and so on, hiding regressions where a different failure occurs.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/AssertAsync.cs:114`

## Problem
AssertAsync.cs:53 says `Expects T (exact type)` and testing.md:37 says `it matches the exact exception type, so catch base types by hand`, but Expect<T> is `catch (T expected) { return expected; }` (AssertAsync.cs:108-117), which matches subclasses. TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync (Tests/Runtime/Support/TestHelpers.cs:130) does the same. Hierarchies that matter: WebSocketException : UHttpException (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketException.cs:9), ObjectDisposedException : InvalidOperationException, BackgroundRequestQueuedException : OperationCanceledException (Runtime/Unity/Mobile/BackgroundNetworkingPolicy.cs:6), HttpFieldValidationException : ArgumentException, every IOException subclass. Uses: 143 ThrowsAsync<UHttpException>, 37 <OperationCanceledException>, 26 <InvalidOperationException>, 20 <IOException>, 17 <ArgumentException>. AssertAsyncTests.cs has no test for a derived or a base type.

**Failure scenario.** Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClientTests.cs:83 expects InvalidOperationException from a second concurrent ReceiveAsync. If the first receive (200 ms token) already ended and the client was torn down, the second call throws ObjectDisposedException, which derives from InvalidOperationException, and the test passes without the concurrent-call guard ever running. The same holds for any `ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>` on an object a regression disposes early.

## Suggested fix
Make Expect<T> compare `ex.GetType() == typeof(T)` as documented and add ThrowsInstanceOfAsync<T> for the call sites that mean a base type (OperationCanceledException vs TaskCanceledException), or change the doc and audit the 26 InvalidOperationException and 20 IOException call sites. Cover both behaviours in AssertAsyncTests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AssertAsync.Expect<T> and TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync compare `ex.GetType() == typeof(T)`, and a ThrowsInstanceOfAsync<T> variant exists for call sites that mean a base type.
- [ ] The call sites of ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>, <IOException>, <OperationCanceledException>, <ArgumentException> and <UHttpException> are audited and each either keeps the exact type or moves to the base-type variant.
- [ ] AssertAsyncTests under Tests/Runtime/  covers a derived type (rejected by ThrowsAsync, accepted by ThrowsInstanceOfAsync) and the exact type.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: Tests/Runtime/AssertAsync.cs:53 documents 'exact type' and Development~/docs/agents/testing.md says 'it matches the exact exception type, so catch base types by hand', but Expect<T> is `catch (T expected) { return expected; }` (AssertAsync.cs:108-123), which accepts subclasses; TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync (Tests/Runtime/Support/TestHelpers.cs:130) too. AssertAsyncTests has no derived/base case; AssertAsyncBoundTests.cs:36-38 even relies on ThrowsAsync<Exception> being a catch-all. So the doc is wrong, not hidden behaviour. Lowered to low: the concrete scenario (WebSocketClientTests.cs:78-83 passing on ObjectDisposedException) needs the client torn down inside a 10 ms window while `await using` still holds it, which I could not make happen from the code; the general risk (ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>/<IOException> passing on a subclass) is real but minor. 136 ThrowsAsync<UHttpException> and 26 <InvalidOperationException> call sites counted.

title: [Testing] UHttpClientTests and UHttpRequestJsonTests leave HttpTransportFactory unregistered, so ConnectionOptionsTests depends on fixture order
body:
## Summary
Both fixtures call HttpTransportFactory.Reset() in TearDown without restoring the default registration, and ConnectionOptionsTests has no SetUp but uses HttpTransportFactory.Default. It passes only because it sorts before the fixtures that reset the factory. A new or renamed fixture, or a different runner order, fails with `No default transport configured` in an unrelated test.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests.cs:266`

## Problem
UHttpClientTests.TearDown (UHttpClientTests.cs:265-269) and UHttpRequestJsonTests.TearDown (UHttpRequestBuilderJsonTests.cs:28-33) call HttpTransportFactory.Reset() and nothing else; after Reset, HttpTransportFactory.Default throws InvalidOperationException (Runtime/Core/HttpTransportFactory.cs:156-168, asserted by DefaultTransportRegistrationTests.cs:127). ConnectionOptionsTests has no SetUp and uses HttpTransportFactory.Default and `new UHttpClient(options)` (ConnectionOptionsTests.cs:12-19). Other fixtures restore the registration (DefaultTransportRegistrationTests.cs:25-33 with the comment `later fixtures (ConnectionOptionsTests has no SetUp) depend on it`, TransportBootstrapTests.cs:34-42, PlatformConfigNoReflectionTests.cs:28-34).

**Failure scenario.** ConnectionOptionsTests passes today only because `ConnectionOptionsTests` sorts before `UHttpClientTests` in namespace TurboHTTP.Tests.Core. A new fixture that uses the default transport and sorts after UHttp* (or a renamed fixture, or a runner that orders differently) fails with `No default transport configured`, pointing at the wrong test.

## Suggested fix
Restore the registration in both TearDowns (TurboHttpBootstrap.RegisterDefaultTransports(), as the other three fixtures do) and give ConnectionOptionsTests its own SetUp that calls RawSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered().

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] UHttpClientTests.TearDown and UHttpRequestJsonTests.TearDown restore the default registration (TurboHttpBootstrap.RegisterDefaultTransports()).
- [ ] ConnectionOptionsTests has its own SetUp that registers the transport (RawSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered()).
- [ ] Running ConnectionOptionsTests after UHttpClientTests in the same run passes (filter-based run recorded in the PR); tests live under Tests/Runtime/Core/.

title: [Testing] FileDownloader progress tests assert on Progress<T> callbacks run on pool threads after a 100 ms sleep with an unsynchronised counter
body:
## Summary
The tests construct Progress<DownloadProgress> inside Task.Run, so callbacks are queued to the thread pool and may run concurrently or out of order. The handlers increment a plain int and the test asserts after Task.Delay(100). A lost increment or a late callback fails the test for reasons unrelated to the downloader.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Files/FileDownloaderTests.cs:279`

## Problem
FileDownloaderTests.cs:200-225 and :232-286 create `new Progress<DownloadProgress>(...)` inside Task.Run, where SynchronizationContext.Current is null, so each Report is queued to the thread pool and callbacks can run concurrently and out of order. The handlers do `lastProgress = p` and `progressCount++` (non-atomic) and the test waits `await Task.Delay(100)` (:223, :279) before asserting `lastProgress != null`, `progressCount >= 3`, `maxBytesDownloaded == 9`. FileDownloader reports per chunk (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:646).

**Failure scenario.** Three chunk reports are queued; two callbacks run at the same time on two pool threads and one increment is lost: progressCount is 2 and `Is.GreaterThanOrEqualTo(3)` fails. Or the pool is busy and the callbacks run after 100 ms: lastProgress is still null. Both are test defects, not downloader defects.

## Suggested fix
Pass a synchronous IProgress<T> implementation (a small class that records under a lock) instead of Progress<T>, and drop the sleep.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The progress tests use a synchronous IProgress<DownloadProgress> implementation that records reports under a lock.
- [ ] The Task.Delay(100) waits are removed from FileDownloaderTests.
- [ ] The tests assert the ordered reports and final byte count deterministically; they live in Tests/Runtime/Files/ and are stable over 200 repeated runs.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Tests/Runtime/Files/FileDownloaderTests.cs:215 and :266 create `new Progress<DownloadProgress>(...)` inside Task.Run (no SynchronizationContext, so Report posts each callback to the thread pool, unordered and possibly concurrent). The handlers do `lastProgress = p` / `progressCount++` / unsynchronised max updates, and the test waits `Task.Delay(100)` (:223, :279) before asserting `lastProgress.BytesDownloaded == content.Length`, `progressCount >= 3`, `maxBytesDownloaded == 9`. FileDownloader reports once per chunk (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:310, :646), so the streaming test gets exactly 3 reports and a single lost increment fails `>= 3`; out-of-order delivery can leave lastProgress at an earlier value in the first test. Test-only race plus a sleep; low.

title: [Testing] Full HTTP/2-over-TLS path on Unity runtimes is covered by one external-network test that also accepts HTTP/1.1 fallback
body:
## Summary
All Http2Connection fixtures run on in-memory duplex streams, and the h2-interop job runs on .NET 8 only. On Unity runtimes (Mono SslStream, BouncyCastle on IL2CPP) the only end-to-end HTTP/2 checks are external-network tests that accept HTTP/1.1 when ALPN is unavailable. A stall in the read loop interacting with BouncyCastleTlsStream (for example an unflushed WINDOW_UPDATE) would pass every automated suite.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Integration/IntegrationTests.cs:603`

## Problem
All Http2Connection/Http2ConnectionManager fixtures run on TestDuplexStream or injected streams. A loopback h2 origin cannot exist in the Editor (Tools~/h2-interop/README.md: Mono SslStream has no ALPN and the vendored BouncyCastle has no TLS server). The only Unity-side end-to-end test is Http2IntegrationCoverage_Phase9_ValidatesAlpnNegotiation (IntegrationTests.cs:600-625) against www.google.com: one buffered GET, with AlpnAssert.UsedHttp2 accepting HTTP/1.1 where the pool's provider has no ALPN (:623-624). The h2-interop rows run on .NET 8 SslStream/BouncyCastle only, and CLAUDE.md marks ALPN as device-only behaviour. testing.md:51-54 lists Mono differences (NetworkStream.ReadAsync ignores cancellation, duplex streams complete synchronously) that these paths depend on.

**Failure scenario.** A regression in the HTTP/2 read loop's interaction with BouncyCastleTlsStream on Mono/IL2CPP (for example a WINDOW_UPDATE that is never flushed because the TLS output backlog is not drained) stalls every large HTTP/2 download in players. Editor suites pass on the duplex stream, CI interop passes on .NET 8, the single ExternalNetwork test downloads a small page and passes.

## Suggested fix
Add ExternalNetwork rows per backend for the cases the interop job has (2 MiB download, 1 MiB upload, 100 concurrent streams, streaming read with cancel) against a host that serves them, assert h2 was really used when the backend is BouncyCastle, and run the same rows in the player smoke with --network. Longer term, add a managed TLS server with ALPN for tests (the shadow-built BouncyCastle server classes in a test-only assembly) so the rows run on loopback.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] [Category("ExternalNetwork")] rows exist per TLS backend for 2 MiB download, 1 MiB upload, 100 concurrent streams and streaming read with cancel, and assert that h2 was used when the backend is BouncyCastle.
- [ ] The same rows run in the player smoke with network enabled, and the results are validated on a device or player build and recorded.
- [ ] Tests live under Tests/Runtime/Integration/; a follow-up issue tracks a managed loopback TLS server with ALPN for tests.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-19` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Core claim holds, with corrections. There are two asserting end-to-end tests, not one: IntegrationTests.cs:603-626 and TlsIntegrationTests.cs:107-129 (HttpClient_Http2_Works). Both use TlsBackend.Auto and AlpnAssert.UsedHttp2, which on a provider that cannot negotiate ALPN asserts usedHttp2 == false and returns (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Tls/AlpnAssert.cs:88-93). Auto resolves to SslStream in the Editor and on iOS/Android (TlsIntegrationTests.cs:95-103) and Mono's SslStream has no ALPN (AlpnAssert.cs:22-27), so on Unity runtimes both tests assert the HTTP/1.1 fallback and never run HTTP/2. HTTP/2 over a real socket does run incidentally in the BouncyCastle rows (TlsIntegrationTests.cs:58-71 HttpClient_WithBouncyCastle_CanFetchGoogle, TlsPublicHostTests.cs:86-97 ValidChain_Succeeds against www.google.com), but they assert only status 200, not that h2 was used; the only h2 assertions with BouncyCastle are handshake-level (BouncyCastleProviderTests.cs:77). A loopback h2 origin is impossible in the Editor: BouncyCastleLoopbackServer is an SslStream server (BouncyCastleLoopbackServer.cs:17-21) and Tools~/h2-interop/README.md:77-78 states it. So flow control, large bodies and concurrent streams over real TLS are covered only on .NET 8 (h2-interop) and by duplex-stream fixtures. Partial overlap with open #99 (device matrix lists HTTP/2 against real servers and BouncyCastle HTTP/2 with 50 concurrent requests), which is a one-time device validation, not regression rows, so not set as known_issue.

Related: #103, #428, #429.

title: [Testing] Unity-side SeededMutator has drifted from the fuzz harness Mutator that docs say is identical
body:
## Summary
Tools~/fuzz/README.md and Mutator.cs state that the Unity regression tests use the same mutator algorithm, but Tests/Runtime/SeededMutator.cs has a different token table and different random draws for byte operations. The same seed produces different inputs, so crashes found by the harness cannot be reproduced in Unity and the Unity tests miss inputs such as `HTTP/1.0 ` and `gzip, chunked`. The doc also cites a stale path.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/SeededMutator.cs:21`

## Problem
Tools~/fuzz/README.md:70 says the Unity tests use `the same mutator` and Tools~/fuzz/Mutator.cs:12 says Tests/Runtime/Fuzzing/SeededMutator.cs `is the same algorithm` (the file is Tests/Runtime/SeededMutator.cs). A diff of the two classes shows a different token table (SeededMutator.cs:21-26 lacks `HTTP/1.0 `, `gzip, chunked`, `Connection: close` and the escaped-quote token) and different random draws for the byte operations (`(byte)Next(256)` vs `(byte)NextULong()`), so the same seed yields different inputs.

**Failure scenario.** A crash found by `run.sh --driver mutate --seed 7` at exec N cannot be reproduced in the Unity runtime by running SeededMutator with seed 7, and the Unity tests never generate the HTTP/1.0 and `gzip, chunked` inputs the harness does, although the README presents the two as equivalent oracles.

## Suggested fix
Compile one mutator source into both (the harness can <Compile Include> Tests/Runtime/SeededMutator.cs as h2-interop does with the adversarial files), or correct the README and the stale path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One mutator source is compiled into both the fuzz harness and the Unity tests, or the README and Mutator.cs comment are corrected to describe the difference and the real path.
- [ ] A test asserts that a fixed seed yields a fixed byte sequence (golden value) in the shared mutator; it lives under Tests/Runtime/.
- [ ] Tools~/fuzz/README.md references the correct file.

title: [Testing] Tests rely on 10 to 100 ms real-time budgets that include socket connect and thread-pool scheduling
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransportTests uses a 100 ms request timeout that must cover loopback connect and response head, WebSocketConnectionPhase18FixesTests runs 25 ms ping and 45 ms pong timeouts with sleeps, and WebSocketClientTests sleeps 10 ms before expecting a concurrent-receive rejection. EarlyDispose_SkipsDrainAndCloses passes whether or not dispose drains. On loaded players or emulators these tests fail for scheduling reasons or fail to detect the regression.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1/RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1655`

## Problem
RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1628-1664 StreamingBodyRead_IgnoresRequestTimeoutAfterHeaders sets a 100 ms request timeout (:1655) that must cover loopback connect, request write and response head before the body phase starts. WebSocketConnectionPhase18FixesTests.cs:66-95 runs PingInterval 25 ms / PongTimeout 45 ms over a transport with a 10 ms delay, sleeps 180 ms and asserts the connection is still Open. WebSocketClientTests.cs:78-83 starts a receive with a 200 ms token, sleeps 10 ms and expects the second ReceiveAsync to be rejected as concurrent. RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1829 cancels a body read after 100 ms and relies on the server's 250 ms delay. RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1761 asserts `Less(elapsed, 1000 ms)` for EarlyDispose_SkipsDrainAndCloses while the server sends the rest of the body after 500 ms, so a dispose that drains (waits 500 ms) passes too.

**Failure scenario.** IL2CPP player on an API 23 x86_64 emulator: connect plus first response head takes 130 ms under load. The 100 ms request timeout fires before headers, SendStreamingAsync throws Timeout and the test fails for a reason unrelated to what it checks. The pong for the 25 ms ping arrives after 60 ms, the 45 ms PongTimeout closes the connection, and KeepAlive_ReceivesPongWithinTightTimeout fails.

## Suggested fix
Use gates instead of clocks: let the scripted server release the body from a TaskCompletionSource after the client reports headers, drive ping/pong through the in-memory peer with a virtual clock or generous timeouts (seconds) where only ordering matters, and assert EarlyDispose by a server that never sends the rest (dispose must still return).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The listed tests use gates (TaskCompletionSource released by the scripted server, in-memory peer with a virtual clock or timeouts of seconds) instead of 10 to 100 ms clocks.
- [ ] EarlyDispose_SkipsDrainAndCloses uses a server that never sends the remaining body, so a draining dispose would hang and fail.
- [ ] Tests under Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1/ and Tests/Runtime/WebSocket/ pass 200 repeated runs under CPU stress; behaviour on a slow emulator is validated on a device or player and recorded.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described: RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1655 sets a 100 ms request timeout that must cover loopback connect + head before a 250 ms server delay; WebSocketConnectionPhase18FixesTests.cs:66-95 uses PingInterval 25 ms / PongTimeout 45 ms over a 10 ms loopback delay and sleeps 180 ms; WebSocketClientTests.cs:78-83 relies on a 10 ms sleep inside a 200 ms token. Whether these fail depends on scheduler load on the player; the journals record passing device/emulator runs, so no observed failure. One static part holds: EarlyDispose (RawSocketTransportTests.cs:1761) asserts dispose < 1000 ms while the server sends the rest after 500 ms, and the response is `Connection: close`, so AcceptCount == 2 is true regardless; a dispose that drains for 500 ms passes. title: [Testing] Tests pin RFC-violating behaviour (obs-fold rejection, unquoted cookie values) and leave Transfer-Encoding identity framing unasserted
body:
## Summary
Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests require a FormatException for obs-fold, which RFC 9112 5.2 says must be replaced with SP, and CookieInterceptorTests require quoted cookie values to be sent back unquoted, contrary to RFC 6265 5.2. The Transfer-Encoding identity test does not assert that the connection is closed, and malformed trailers are skipped while the same line in headers is rejected. A runtime fix for the protocol bugs has to fight its own suite.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:242`

## Problem
Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:242-253: Parse_ObsFoldContinuationLine_ThrowsFormatException and Parse_ObsFoldWithTab_ThrowsFormatException require a FormatException for an obs-fold in a response; RFC 9112 5.2 says a user agent MUST replace a received obs-fold with SP before interpreting the value (runtime side reported as http1-protocol-05). CookieInterceptorTests.cs:452-469 CookieJar_UnquotesCookieValues requires `token="abc"` to be sent back as `token=abc`; RFC 6265 5.2 stores the value as received (runtime side mw-protocol-07). Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:597-605 Parse_TransferEncodingIdentity_TreatedAsAbsent sends `Transfer-Encoding: identity` with Content-Length and asserts only the body text, not that the connection is closed afterwards, which is the one property the runtime comment promises for this smuggling-shaped message (Http11ResponseParser.cs:498-499; RFC 9112 6.3 item 3). Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:209-224 Parse_ChunkedBody_MalformedTrailers_AreSkipped accepts a trailer line without a colon that the same parser rejects in the header section (:277 of the strictness tests).

**Failure scenario.** A server behind an old proxy sends a folded header. The client fails the whole response with a FormatException instead of unfolding, and the test suite asserts that this is correct, so whoever implements the MUST sees two red tests and has no test describing the conformant result.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 5.2, RFC 9112 6.3, RFC 6265 5.2

## Suggested fix
Rewrite the two obs-fold tests to assert the unfolded value (and the second case's resulting framing), change the cookie test to expect the quoted value, add `KeepAlive == false` to the identity test, and decide one rule for malformed field lines in trailers and headers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The obs-fold tests assert the unfolded value per RFC 9112 5.2 (and the resulting framing for the tab case).
- [ ] The cookie test expects the quoted value to be sent back as received (RFC 6265 5.2).
- [ ] Parse_TransferEncodingIdentity_TreatedAsAbsent also asserts KeepAlive == false (RFC 9112 6.3).
- [ ] One documented rule exists for malformed field lines in trailers versus headers, with tests in Tests/Runtime/Transport/ covering it. The tests fail against the current runtime where it is non-conformant, or are tied to the runtime fix issues.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-25` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Two of the four sub-claims are real RFC deviations pinned by tests; both are the test-side mirror of runtime findings already verified in other batches (http1-protocol-05 confirmed low, mw-protocol-07 confirmed medium), so this adds no new defect, only the note that the fix must change tests. (1) Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:241-253 require FormatException for obs-fold; runtime Http11ResponseParser.cs:701-702 throws; RFC 9112 5.2 says a user agent MUST replace obs-fold with SP (reject is allowed only for servers and proxies). (2) CookieInterceptorTests.cs:452-469 requires token="abc" to be returned as token=abc via CookieJar.cs:383,787-796; RFC 6265 5.2 has no unquoting step. (3) Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:596-605 asserts only the body for Transfer-Encoding: identity + Content-Length; the close is asserted only for chunked + Content-Length (StrictnessTests.cs:165-176), so the identity branch's faultyFraming close (Http11ResponseParser.cs:453, 315) is unpinned: a missing assertion, not a wrong one. (4) Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:209-224 pins lenient skipping of malformed trailer lines; this is a documented deliberate asymmetry (Http11ResponseParser.cs:693-694 'Unlike the lenient trailer path') and RFC 9110 6.5 lets a recipient discard trailers, so it is not forbidden behaviour. Severity low: the title's 'RFCs forbid' applies to (1) and (2) only, and those are tracked as runtime findings.

title: [Testing] TestDuplexStream parks a pool thread per pending read and 159 HTTP/2 tests dispose the connection only on the success path
body:
## Summary
BlockingStream.ReadAsyncCore blocks a thread-pool thread in TryTake(Timeout.Infinite) for every pending read, and 159 Http2 tests call `conn.Dispose()` as their last statement. When an assertion fails first, the connection and its read loop stay alive with a blocked pool thread. A genuine regression can then cascade into failures in unrelated fixtures that use the same harness, hiding the root cause.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Helpers/TestDuplexStream.cs:141`

## Problem
BlockingStream.ReadAsyncCore runs `Task.Run(() => _chunks.TryTake(out chunk, Timeout.Infinite, cancellationToken))` (TestDuplexStream.cs:137-153): a blocking wait on a pool thread for as long as the read is pending, i.e. one thread per idle Http2Connection read loop plus one per pending server-side ReadFrameAsync. In Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2, 159 tests end with a plain `conn.Dispose();` as the last statement, 6 use `using var conn` and 5 dispose in finally. When an assertion throws first, the connection is never disposed, its read-loop token is never cancelled and the TryTake never returns. testing.md:78 requires `using var` for clients and responses. The same harness backs InMemoryWebSocketPeer.

**Failure scenario.** A real regression fails 20 HTTP/2 tests in one PlayMode run. Each leaves a pool thread blocked forever; Mono injects new pool threads slowly, so later fixtures with 100-300 ms windows (finding 05) and the WebSocket tests on the same harness start failing too. The report shows 60 failures across unrelated fixtures and the root cause is hidden.

## Suggested fix
Implement the pending read with a TaskCompletionSource/SemaphoreSlim signalled by Write and CompleteWriting (no blocked thread), and have CreateInitializedConnectionAsync return a disposable scope used with `await using`/`using` so the connection and both stream ends are torn down on every path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TestDuplexStream's pending read uses a TaskCompletionSource or SemaphoreSlim signalled by Write and CompleteWriting, with no blocked thread.
- [ ] CreateInitializedConnectionAsync returns a disposable scope and tests use `using`/`await using` so connection and both stream ends are disposed on every path.
- [ ] A test in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/ shows that a failing assertion leaves no live read loop or blocked pool thread.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described: BlockingStream.ReadAsyncCore parks a pool thread in `_chunks.TryTake(out chunk, Timeout.Infinite, cancellationToken)` inside Task.Run (TestDuplexStream.cs:137-153); in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2 I count 159 trailing `conn.Dispose();`, 6 `using var conn`, 5 dispose-in-finally; the fixture TearDown (Http2ConnectionTests.LeakCheck.cs:16-20) only checks streaming responses and disposes no connection. Partial refutation of 'forever': a leaked connection with an open stream is torn down by the keep-alive PING (Http2Options defaults 30 s interval + 10 s timeout, Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:24-25; Http2Connection.Liveness.cs:11 'only while streams are open'), releasing the thread after about 40 s; only stream-less leaked connections stay parked. The cascade (later fixtures failing from pool starvation) depends on Mono/IL2CPP thread injection and only arises once tests already fail, so plausible and low.

Related: [[R11-tests-quality-06]].

title: [Testing] In-memory HTTP/2, WebSocket and fuzz harnesses deliver each write in one read, so split frame headers are never tested
body:
## Summary
TestDuplexStream queues one chunk per Write and a read returns that chunk, InMemoryWebSocketPeer writes each frame once, and the fuzz targets feed whole inputs from MemoryStream. Only four HTTP/1.1 parser tests exercise fragmented reads. A read loop that assumes a frame header arrives in one ReadAsync would pass every unit test and fail over TLS where records split frames arbitrarily.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Helpers/TestDuplexStream.cs:162`

## Problem
TestDuplexStream.BlockingStream queues one byte[] per Write (:101-107) and a read drains the current chunk up to `count` (:162-169). Http2FrameCodec writes the 9-byte header and the payload as separate writes (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2FrameCodec.cs:221, :229), so the client always receives a whole frame header in one read and a payload in at most the writer's slices. InMemoryWebSocketPeer builds each frame in a MemoryStream and writes it once (InMemoryWebSocketPeer.cs:85-101) over the same TestDuplexStream. Http2FrameCodecTests use MemoryStream. Fuzz: Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:74, :216, :354 feed MemoryStream and H2FuzzStream.ReadAsync returns Math.Min(buffer.Length, remaining) (H2FuzzStream.cs:76-81); only h1-chunked-body varies the caller's buffer size, not the transport read size. Read fragmentation exists only in Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:70 FragmentedReadStream (4 tests: :762, :791, :806, :824). No test double models partial writes or a slow reader except GatedWriteStream. Real segmentation is seen only by the .NET 8 interop rows and the manual Autobahn run.

**Failure scenario.** A change to the HTTP/2 read loop or WebSocketFrameReader reads the header with a single ReadAsync and treats a short read as complete (works when the 9 or 2-14 header bytes arrive together). All ~600 Http2ConnectionTests/WebSocket unit tests and all fuzz targets pass; over TLS on a device, where records split frames at arbitrary offsets, the connection fails with a bogus frame length.

## Suggested fix
Give TestDuplexStream an optional read-size schedule (seeded sizes 1..N, as FragmentedReadStream has) and run the HTTP/2 connection and WebSocket fixtures, or at least the adversarial scenarios and one test per frame type, with 1-byte and prime-sized reads; make the fuzz targets take the read size from the first input byte for h1-response, h2-frames, h2-connection and ws-frames as h1-chunked-body already does.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TestDuplexStream supports a seeded read-size schedule (1..N bytes) and the HTTP/2 connection and WebSocket fixtures run at least one test per frame type with 1-byte and prime-sized reads.
- [ ] The h1-response, h2-frames, h2-connection and ws-frames fuzz targets take the read size from the first input byte, as h1-chunked-body does.
- [ ] A regression test in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/ fails against a read loop that treats a short header read as complete.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: TestDuplexStream.BlockingStream queues one byte[] per Write (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Helpers/TestDuplexStream.cs:101-107) and a read drains the current chunk (:162-169); Http2FrameCodec writes the 9-byte header and payload slices as separate writes (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2FrameCodec.cs:221, :229), so a frame header is never split; InMemoryWebSocketPeer writes each frame once (InMemoryWebSocketPeer.cs:85-101); fuzz targets feed MemoryStream (Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:74, :216, :354) and H2FuzzStream returns Math.Min(buffer.Length, remaining) (H2FuzzStream.cs:76-81); only h1-chunked-body varies the caller buffer (Targets.cs:108). The only read-fragmenting double I found is FragmentedReadStream (Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:70). Overstated on two points: header/payload boundaries and payload slices are exercised, and the CI h2-interop/tls-interop rows run the same read loops over real TLS records. Production reads go through ReadExactAsync loops (Http2FrameCodec.cs:117, :136, :255; WebSocketFrameReader.cs:88-289), so the gap is in regression protection, not a current defect. Low.

title: [Testing] Negative HTTP/2 and transport tests discard ThrowsAsync<UHttpException> results and accept unrelated exception types
body:
## Summary
About 21 negative tests call ThrowsAsync<UHttpException> and discard the result, and six more accept any of three unrelated exception types. They pass for any UHttpException, so a wrong error type, a wrong HTTP/2 error code or a broken setup still reads as a pass. This is the same pattern issue #451 fixes for TLS negative rows, in the HTTP/2, transport and file-downloader tests.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:83`

## Problem
21 call sites discard the result of ThrowsAsync<UHttpException>, e.g. FrameHandling.cs:83 (GoAwayFrame_FailsHigherStreams), :162, :200 (RstStreamFrame_FailsSpecificStream), ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:149, :399, :434, AdditionalCoverage.cs:576, StreamingResponses.cs:570, ConnectionSetup.cs:760, RawSocketTransportHttp2ConnectionManagementTests.cs:218 and :378, RawSocketTransportTests.cs:2335, RawSocketTransportProxy407Tests.cs:113, FileDownloaderResumeSafetyTests.cs:75 and :469. Six more tests accept three types as equivalent: `catch (Http2ProtocolException) { } catch (UHttpException) { } catch (ObjectDisposedException) { }` (Http2FlowControlTests.cs:876-881 and 2 more there, AdditionalCoverage.cs 2 tests, ProtocolAndCleanup.cs 1 test). CLAUDE.md section 3 says network/protocol failures are UHttpException(UHttpError); these tests accept a raw internal Http2ProtocolException or ObjectDisposedException from the dispatch path as correct.

**Failure scenario.** GoAwayFrame_FailsHigherStreams: RFC 9113 6.8 makes streams above last-stream-id unprocessed and safe to retry. A regression that fails them with a non-retryable error type (or with UHttpErrorType.Unknown wrapping a NullReferenceException from cleanup) still throws UHttpException and the test passes; RetryInterceptor then stops retrying GOAWAY-refused requests in production. RstStreamFrame_FailsSpecificStream neither checks the mapped error nor that the connection stays alive.

## Spec reference
RFC 9113 6.8

## Suggested fix
Assert ex.HttpError.Type and, for protocol errors, the inner exception type and the frame the client sent (RST_STREAM/GOAWAY code); for GOAWAY/REFUSED_STREAM assert the retryability flag. Replace the three-type catch ladders with one expected type.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each listed negative test asserts ex.HttpError.Type, and for protocol errors the inner exception type and the RST_STREAM/GOAWAY code the client sent.
- [ ] GOAWAY and REFUSED_STREAM tests assert the retryability flag.
- [ ] Three-type catch ladders are replaced by one expected exception type.
- [ ] Mutating the production error type or code makes at least one converted test fail; checked in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/ and Tests/Runtime/Transport/.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: 12 statement-level `AssertAsync.ThrowsAsync<UHttpException>(` plus several awaited `TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync<UHttpException>(` discard the exception (e.g. Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:83, :200; ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:149, :399, :434; AdditionalCoverage.cs:576; RawSocketTransportProxy407Tests.cs:113; FileDownloaderResumeSafetyTests.cs:75, :469), and the three-type catch ladders exist (Http2FlowControlTests.cs:880-882, :936-938, :997-999; AdditionalCoverage.cs:321-327, :374-380; ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:849-854). The stated consequence is partly refuted: GOAWAY/REFUSED_STREAM retryability is asserted elsewhere (Http2ConnectionTests.ConnectionManagement.cs:290-291 expects Http2RetryableRequestException with RequestNotProcessed; RawSocketTransportHttp2ConnectionManagementTests GoAwayMidBurst_InFlightPosts_AllSucceed :254 and RefusedStream_PostIsReplayedTransparently :225; adversarial 'goaway/refused-stream-burst'), and RST_STREAM mapping is asserted by the sibling RstStreamCancel_FrameFailsSpecificStreamAsNetworkError (FrameHandling.cs:205). The flow-control ladders do assert the GOAWAY error code first (Http2FlowControlTests.cs:869-874). So these are weak, partly redundant tests rather than a coverage hole: low. #451 tracks only the TLS rows (AuthenticationException), not these, so known_issue stays 0.

title: [Testing] Three HTTP/2 negative tests cannot fail because their assertion sits inside try/catch (Exception) { }
body:
## Summary
SettingsAck_NonZeroPayload_FrameSizeError, SettingsAck_OnNonZeroStream_ProtocolError and FailAllStreams_PreventsNewStreamCreation put their only assertion inside a try block with an empty catch (Exception). NUnit's AssertionException is swallowed, so the tests pass whatever the connection does. Protocol-error handling for SETTINGS ACK with a payload or on a non-zero stream is therefore untested.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:452`

## Problem
FrameHandling.cs:414-463 SettingsAck_NonZeroPayload_FrameSizeError: `try { await initTask; await Task.Delay(500); Assert.IsFalse(conn.IsAlive); } catch (Exception) { }`. Http2ConnectionTests.ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:252-301 SettingsAck_OnNonZeroStream_ProtocolError has the same block (290-298). Http2ConnectionTests.AdditionalCoverage.cs:565-572 FailAllStreams_PreventsNewStreamCreation: `try { await task1; Assert.Fail("Expected exception"); } catch (Exception) { }`. Unity's NUnit (com.unity.ext.nunit 1.0.6, NUnit 3.5: no Assert.Multiple, testing.md:42) reports an assertion only through the thrown AssertionException, and the body runs under Task.Run, so the swallowed exception leaves the test green. Neither SETTINGS test reads the GOAWAY frame, and rg finds no other test for these two cases (a script over every try/catch in Tests/ found exactly these three swallowing blocks).

**Failure scenario.** Http2Connection stops validating a SETTINGS ACK with a non-zero length (RFC 9113 6.5: connection error FRAME_SIZE_ERROR) or a SETTINGS frame on stream 1 (PROTOCOL_ERROR) and keeps the connection alive. Both tests still pass: Assert.IsFalse(conn.IsAlive) throws, the catch discards it. In FailAllStreams, a request that wrongly succeeds after the connection error hits Assert.Fail, which is discarded the same way.

## Spec reference
RFC 9113 6.5

## Suggested fix
Await the outcome outside the catch: read the client's GOAWAY from serverCodec and assert its error code (as IdleStreamAndPreface.cs:59 does with ReadGoAwayErrorCode), and replace the try/catch with TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync<UHttpException>. Add a check_repo rule or a grep gate for `catch (Exception)` blocks without rethrow that follow an Assert in Tests/.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The three tests read the client GOAWAY from serverCodec and assert its error code (FRAME_SIZE_ERROR or PROTOCOL_ERROR as RFC 9113 requires), using TestHelpers.AssertThrowsAsync<UHttpException> instead of try/catch.
- [ ] No empty catch (Exception) remains around assertions in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/.
- [ ] A check_repo rule or grep gate rejects assertion-swallowing catch (Exception) blocks in Tests/.
- [ ] Each test fails when the production error handling is removed (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:452-460 and Http2ConnectionTests.ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:290-298: `try { await initTask; await Task.Delay(500); Assert.IsFalse(conn.IsAlive); } catch (Exception) { }`. Either initTask throws (correct client, caught) or the assertion throws AssertionException (broken client, also caught); the test passes both ways and reads no GOAWAY. rg finds no other test that sends a SETTINGS ACK with payload or on a non-zero stream (all other `Flags = Http2FrameFlags.Ack` sites are valid handshakes), and the Adversarial scenarios do not cover them, so RFC 9113 6.5 FRAME_SIZE_ERROR / PROTOCOL_ERROR on SETTINGS ACK has no effective test. title: [Testing] Pooled-buffer and streaming-response leak checks run in only one or two fixtures
body:
## Summary
The streaming-response leak check is wired into Http2ConnectionTests only, and the ByteArrayPool outstanding count is asserted in one more fixture. About 20 other test files create streaming responses or rent pooled buffers without checking that they were returned. Buffer and body ownership bugs on error paths in the HTTP/1.1 transport, proxy, WebSocket, decompression and cache code would not be caught.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ConnectionTests.LeakCheck.cs:9`

## Problem
StreamingResponseLeakCheck.Begin/AssertNoLeakSince is wired into SetUp/TearDown of Http2ConnectionTests only (LeakCheck.cs:9-20; the other user tests the counter itself), while about 20 other test files create streaming responses (rg SendStreamingAsync|UHttpStreamingResponse: RawSocketTransportTests, RawSocketTransportProxyTunnelTests, DecompressionInterceptorTests, UHttpClientTests.Execution, PluginInterceptorCapabilityTests, ...). ByteArrayPool.GetDiagnostics().ActiveCount, the documented leak oracle (Runtime/Core/Internal/ByteArrayPool.cs:24-27, #292), is read only by ByteArrayPoolLeakDetectionTests and SoakShortTests. The fixtures themselves break the ownership rule that would make a suite-wide check possible: 43 `var client = new UHttpClient(...)` without using (FileDownloaderTests.cs 15) and 33 buffered responses assigned without using (IntegrationTests.cs 7, MockHttpServerTests.cs 6, RawSocketTransportTests.cs 5); ByteArrayPoolLeakDetectionTests.cs:24-33 has to drain finalizers because of them. The full leak verdict is the manual, .NET-only soak workflow.

**Failure scenario.** A change to Http11ResponseBodySource skips ByteArrayPool.Return on the cancel-mid-chunk path, or returns a buffer twice on the proxy 407 retry path. Every RawSocketTransport/Proxy/WebSocket test passes because none compares the pool's outstanding count before and after; the double return corrupts a later response body on a device, the missing return shows up only if someone dispatches the 1 h soak.

## Suggested fix
Add a shared fixture base (or SetUp/TearDown helper) that snapshots ByteArrayPool ActiveCount, the ObjectPool outstanding counters and the streaming-response counter and asserts a zero delta, and apply it to the HTTP/1.1 transport, proxy, HTTP/2 manager, WebSocket connection, decompression and cache-streaming fixtures. Fix the undisposed clients/responses first so the delta is meaningful.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A shared fixture base or SetUp/TearDown helper snapshots ByteArrayPool ActiveCount, the ObjectPool outstanding counters and the streaming-response counter and asserts a zero delta.
- [ ] The helper is applied to the HTTP/1.1 transport, proxy, HTTP/2 manager, WebSocket connection, decompression and cache fixtures.
- [ ] A deliberately leaked buffer in a test fails the helper (Tests/Runtime/Core/ or the relevant area folder).
- [ ] Leaks the new check exposes are fixed or filed as separate issues.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Verified: StreamingResponseLeakCheck is used only by Http2ConnectionTests.LeakCheck.cs:13/:19 and the counter's own test (UHttpStreamingResponseLeakCounterTests.cs:43-72); ByteArrayPool.GetDiagnostics().ActiveCount (leak oracle per Runtime/Core/Internal/ByteArrayPool.cs:24-27) is read only in ByteArrayPoolLeakDetectionTests and Tools~/soak/SoakClient.cs:93/:301; SoakShortTests.cs:38-67 checks ParsedResponsePool/HeaderParseScratchPool. 41 `var client = new UHttpClient(` lines without using (15 in FileDownloaderTests.cs). Slightly overstated: targeted pool tests exist (Http2ConnectionTests.PoolLeakUnderStall.cs, ObjectPoolDiscardAccountingTests, ByteArrayPoolLeakDetectionTests on the abandon path) and the soak harness checks all pools, but no HTTP/1.1 transport, proxy, WebSocket, decompression or cache fixture asserts a zero pool delta. A missing suite-wide oracle is a coverage recommendation, not a defect: low.

title: [Testing] Tests use fixed Task.Delay sleeps as synchronisation and then assert state, against the determinism rule
body:
## Summary
Tests in Http2FlowControlTests, Http2ConnectionTests, WebSocketConnectionTests, CacheInterceptorTests.Streaming and FileDownloader tests wait a fixed 50 to 500 ms and then assert a state. On a slow player the assertion runs too early, and for must-not-happen checks the sleep makes the test pass vacuously. This violates the project rule against wall-clock sleeps as synchronization.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2FlowControlTests.cs:213`

## Problem
Positive assertion after a fixed sleep: Http2FlowControlTests.cs:213 and :300 (`await Task.Delay(300); Assert.IsFalse(conn.IsAlive)`), :151 (100 ms, then only IsAlive); Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:507, :555, :595 (200 ms); ProtocolAndCleanup.cs:736 and AdditionalCoverage.cs (100-200 ms, then reflection on _activeStreams); WebSocketConnectionTests.cs:98 (50 ms, then State == Closed and CloseStatus); CacheInterceptorTests.Streaming.cs:100 and :242 (50 ms, then storage count); FileDownloaderTests.cs:223 and :279 (100 ms, then progress values). Negative `still pending after N ms` checks: TcpConnectionPoolTests.cs:292, :399, :420; AdditionalCoverage.cs:57 and :448; CacheInterceptorTests.VariantsAndAsync.cs:489, :531; WebSocketReconnectionTests.cs:78, :148. testing.md:32 forbids this (`no wall-clock sleeps as synchronization`). The HTTP/2 cases run on TestDuplexStream, where every pending read blocks a pool thread (finding 10), and 138 nested blocking AssertAsync.ThrowsAsync calls inside async bodies add to the pool pressure.

**Failure scenario.** On a 2-core Android emulator lane (run-emulator-tests.sh --jobs 2) the thread pool is saturated by blocked duplex reads; the read loop processes the zero WINDOW_UPDATE 400 ms after it was written. WindowUpdate_Zero_ConnectionDies checks IsAlive at 300 ms and fails although the client is correct. In the other direction, CacheInterceptorTests.Streaming.cs:100 asserts `storage count == 0` 50 ms after an abandoned stream: a regression that stores the truncated body 80 ms later passes that assertion.

## Suggested fix
Wait on the observable event instead: read the GOAWAY/RST_STREAM frame from serverCodec, await a completion source the fake storage or handler sets, or poll with a bounded WaitUntil helper for positive conditions. For `must not happen` checks, drive the next deterministic step (send the frame that would unblock) rather than a time window.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Positive-condition waits use the observable event (a frame read from serverCodec, a completion source set by the fake) or a bounded WaitUntil helper, with no fixed Task.Delay before an assertion.
- [ ] Must-not-happen checks drive the next deterministic step instead of sleeping.
- [ ] A grep gate or check_repo rule flags Task.Delay followed by an assertion in Tests/ outside an allow-list.
- [ ] Converted tests pass 100 consecutive runs under CPU load (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/, WebSocket/, Cache/).

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced the cited sites: Http2FlowControlTests.cs:213-214 and :300-301 (`await Task.Delay(300); Assert.IsFalse(conn.IsAlive)`), Http2ConnectionTests.FrameHandling.cs:507-508 (200 ms), CacheInterceptorTests.Streaming.cs:100-102 (50 ms then storage count == 0, a vacuous negative), WebSocketConnectionTests.cs:98-102 (50 ms then State/CloseStatus), TcpConnectionPoolTests.cs:292-293 (100 ms then `IsFalse(task.IsCompleted)`). 132 Task.Delay calls in Tests/Runtime in total (not all are synchronisation). This contradicts testing.md 'Deterministic only: no wall-clock sleeps as synchronization'. No guard refutes it; the same fixtures already have deterministic alternatives (WaitForConditionAsync, reading the GOAWAY from serverCodec). The device-failure half is runtime dependent, the vacuous-negative half is static. Medium as a rule violation spread over the HTTP/2, cache and WebSocket fixtures; each single site is low.

title: [Testing] 324 test bodies in 47 files wait with Task.Run(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult() instead of AssertAsync

## Summary

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/TcpConnectionPoolTests.cs:391`

## Problem
testing.md:68-71: `Direct Task.Run(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult() has no bound: use AssertAsync`. `rg '^\s*\}\)\.GetAwaiter\(\)\.GetResult\(\);' Tests` finds 324 sites in 47 files, among them fixtures on real sockets and the public network: TcpConnectionPoolTests.cs (27, e.g. :391 MaxConnectionsPerHost_BlocksWhenAtLimit awaits a lease with CancellationToken.None), Http11ResponseParserTests.cs (40), Http11SerializerTests.cs (33), Http2FrameCodecTests.cs (16), IntegrationTests.cs (13, incl. ExternalNetwork at :583), OAuthClientTests.cs (10), ConcurrencyLimiterTests.cs (10), HappyEyeballsTests.cs (6), SslStreamProviderTests.cs and BouncyCastleProviderTests.cs (ExternalNetwork handshakes). Tools~/ci/check_repo.py has rules for Assert.*Async and async Task tests (check_unity_nunit, :179-218) but none for this pattern; tests are outside the banned-symbol analyzers (shadow_build.py:306-308).

Convert the 324 sites to AssertAsync.Run (mechanical: `Task.Run(async () => {...}).GetAwaiter().GetResult()` -> `AssertAsync.Run(async () => {...})`) and add a check_repo `unitynunit` rule that rejects `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` in Tests/ outside AssertAsync.cs and the documented sync stream doubles.

- [ ] All 324 sites are converted to AssertAsync.Run(async () => {...}).

title: [Testing] PublicChain_ProductionConfiguration_IsTrustedByPlatformRootStore fails on Android from 2026-11-27 when its committed leaf expires
body:
## Summary
The test verifies the committed www.digicert.com leaf at a fixed verification time of 2026-11-01, but the leaf expires on 2026-11-26. On Android the platform verifier drops the verification time argument, so after that date the real clock makes the test fail. The test is not gated on Android and is not in the Player-Android skip baseline.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Tls/ServerCertificateVerifierTests.cs:191`

## Problem
The test verifies the committed www.digicert.com leaf at a fixed time 2026-11-01 (ServerCertificateVerifierTests.cs:195-198); PublicChainTestCertificates.cs:18 gives LeafNotAfterUtc 2026-11-26T23:59:59Z. SetUp skips only Linux (:27-28) and the test has no RequireTestAnchorVerifier call, and Tools~/unity/skip-baseline.txt does not list it among the 16 Player-Android skips, so it runs there. On Android the platform verifier is AndroidTrustManagerVerifier.Verify, which drops verificationTimeUtc (`return Evaluate(chainDer, host)`, Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/AndroidTrustManagerVerifier.cs:49-64; doc :25 `The platform evaluates at the current time`). That verifier is installed only inside a BouncyCastle handshake (TurboTlsAuthentication.cs:75-77); without it ServerCertificateVerifier.Verify returns NoVerifier (ServerCertificateVerifier.cs:293-294). Windows, macOS and iOS verifiers honour the passed time.

**Failure scenario.** From 2026-11-27 an Android device or emulator run evaluates the leaf at the current date, X509TrustManagerExtensions throws CertificateExpiredException, the result is NotTimeValid and the test fails on every run until the chain is re-captured. Before that date, `run-device-tests.sh --filter ServerCertificateVerifierTests` runs the fixture without any earlier BouncyCastle handshake, no verifier is registered and the test fails with NoVerifier.

## Suggested fix
Gate the test with TestRequirements.IgnoreEnvironment on platforms whose verifier cannot take a verification time (Android), or register the Android verifier in SetUp and assert Trusted only while DateTime.UtcNow is inside the leaf validity (NotTimeValid afterwards). Add a guard test like TestShortLivedLocalhostCertificateTests that fails 30 days before LeafNotAfterUtc where wall-clock validity matters.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The test is gated with TestRequirements.IgnoreEnvironment on platforms whose verifier cannot take a verification time (Android), or it asserts Trusted only while DateTime.UtcNow is inside the leaf validity and NotTimeValid afterwards.
- [ ] A guard test fails ahead of the leaf expiry so the chain is re-captured in time.
- [ ] The Android run is recorded as validated on an emulator or device.
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Transport/Tls/ simulating a clock after NotAfter.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-13` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ServerCertificateVerifierTests.cs:191-207 verifies the committed leaf at a fixed 2026-11-01; PublicChainTestCertificates.cs:18 LeafNotAfterUtc = 2026-11-26T23:59:59Z (11 days after this review). SetUp skips only Linux (:27-28); the test has no RequireTestAnchorVerifier call and is not among the 16 Player-Android skips (Tools~/unity/skip-baseline.txt), and the phone run in 2026-11-player-ready-tests.md ran the fixture with only the 8 test-anchor cases skipped, so it executes on Android. With no test anchors, ServerCertificateVerifier.Verify (ServerCertificateVerifier.cs:288-296) calls the platform verifier; on Android that is AndroidTrustManagerVerifier.Verify, which discards verificationTimeUtc (`return Evaluate(chainDer, host)`, AndroidTrustManagerVerifier.cs:49-64; remark :25 'The platform evaluates at the current time'), while Apple/macOS/Windows verifiers pass the time through (AppleTrustVerifier.cs:67, MacSecTrustVerifier.cs:119-124). So from 2026-11-27 every Android player run fails this test until the chain is re-captured. The ordering half also holds statically: the Android verifier is registered only at TurboTlsAuthentication.cs:75-77 (sole caller of EnsureRegistered), so a filtered run with no earlier BouncyCastle handshake gets NoVerifier (:293-294). The Android TrustManager rejecting an expired leaf is standard platform behaviour; needs-device confirmation only for the exact status. No open issue tracks it (#239/#99 are about device validation, not this expiry).

## Summary
Nine blocks in eight test files are guarded by TURBOHTTP_INTEGRATION_TESTS, and two files by TURBOHTTP_USE_SYSTEM_TEXT_JSON. The shadow build never defines these symbols, so the code compiles only in the host-editor ExternalNetwork run, where a single compile error hides every result. Breakage reaches main unnoticed.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Transport/Tls/TlsIntegrationTests.cs:1`

## Problem
Blocks: TlsIntegrationTests.cs:1, TlsPublicHostTests.cs:1, TlsPerformanceBenchmarkTests.cs:1, BouncyCastleProviderTests.cs:45 and :206, SslStreamProviderTests.cs:45, Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:697, TcpConnectionPoolTests.cs:776, RawSocketTransportTests.cs:2447; UHttpClientTests.Builders.cs:162 and Runtime/JSON/JsonRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:101 for TURBOHTTP_USE_SYSTEM_TEXT_JSON. Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:69-82 defines TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE and TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING for every variant but neither of these two symbols, and run-tests.sh:121-124 adds the integration define only for --integration/--category ExternalNetwork. Compile the test assemblies a second time in the shadow build with TURBOHTTP_INTEGRATION_TESTS (and one variant with TURBOHTTP_USE_SYSTEM_TEXT_JSON if that option stays supported), compile-only. Better: drop the define and gate these tests by category only, as IntegrationTests.cs already does.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

title: [Testing] PCM decoders and the SegmentedBuffer family that handle peer-controlled data or pooled buffers have no direct tests
body:
## Summary
AiffPcmDecoder has no references in Tests/, WavPcmDecoder has a single happy-path test, and SegmentedBuffer, SegmentedReadStream, PooledSegment, ReadOnlySequenceStream and PooledArrayBufferWriter have no fixtures of their own. These types parse peer-controlled binary or own pooled buffers, so truncated chunks and double-dispose bugs would go unnoticed.

## Location
- `Tests/Runtime/Unity/AudioPipelineV2Tests.cs:41`

## Problem
Counted with rg over Tests/: AiffPcmDecoder (Runtime/Unity/Decoders/AiffPcmDecoder.cs, 255 lines) 0 references; WavPcmDecoder (225 lines) one happy-path test (AudioPipelineV2Tests.cs:41) and no truncated/oversized chunk case; the Core pooled-buffer primitives SegmentedBuffer (236 lines), SegmentedReadStream (247), PooledSegment (94), ReadOnlySequenceStream (112), PooledArrayBufferWriter (248) have no fixture of their own (only indirect use; PooledSegment and ReadOnlySequenceStream are never named in Tests/); AndroidTrustManagerVerifier (319 lines, JNI trust decision) 0 references, also in the device fixtures under Tests/Runtime/Mobile; PoolHealthReporter (231 lines) 0; TrailerFieldValidator only through one parser test. Tests/Runtime/Performance/RequestQueueTests.cs is 34 lines for the 223-line RequestQueue. HpackHuffmanTests.cs:105-113 Decode_TruncatedInput_Throws is an empty method.

**Failure scenario.** A WAV or AIFF response with a chunk size of 0xFFFFFFF0 or a sample count that overflows int reaches the decoder from the network through AudioClipHandler. No test feeds a malformed file, so an IndexOutOfRangeException, a multi-gigabyte allocation or an endless loop in chunk skipping ships unnoticed. A double Dispose of SegmentedBuffer that returns segments twice is caught by no unit test either.

## Suggested fix
Add table-driven tests for both PCM decoders (truncated header, chunk size past EOF, zero channels, odd sizes, huge counts) and unit fixtures for the SegmentedBuffer family (write/advance across segment edges, ToArray, Reset, double Dispose, read stream at every boundary) with the ByteArrayPool delta asserted. Add a device-only fixture for AndroidTrustManagerVerifier (trusted public chain, expired, untrusted, malformed DER).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Table-driven tests for both PCM decoders cover truncated header, chunk size past EOF, zero channels, odd sizes and huge counts, each with a defined error.
- [ ] Unit fixtures for the SegmentedBuffer family cover writes and advances across segment edges, ToArray, Reset, double Dispose and reads at every boundary.
- [ ] The fixtures assert a zero ByteArrayPool delta.
- [ ] Tests live in Tests/Runtime/Unity/ and Tests/Runtime/Core/ and fail when the bounds checks are removed.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-18` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Counts re-run with rg -w over Tests/: AiffPcmDecoder 0, PooledSegment 0, ReadOnlySequenceStream 0, AndroidTrustManagerVerifier 0, PoolHealthReporter 0, TrailerFieldValidator 0 by name; WavPcmDecoder 1 (happy path only, Tests/Runtime/Unity/AudioPipelineV2Tests.cs:41-52); SegmentedReadStream only in CoreSurfaceTests.cs:29 (type-name check); SegmentedBuffer only as a helper in cache/decompression tests; Tests/Runtime/Performance/RequestQueueTests.cs is 34 lines with one test; Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/HpackHuffmanTests.cs:104-113 Decode_TruncatedInput_Throws has an empty body. Both PCM decoders are registered by default (Runtime/Unity/Decoders/DecoderRegistry.cs:421-422), so they parse network bytes. The gap is concrete: WavPcmDecoder.cs:73 computes chunkDataOffset + chunkSize in unchecked int, so a chunk size near int.MaxValue passes the bounds check and is only stopped because the next loop turn slices at a negative offset (:67) and the catch-all at :42 wraps it; nothing pins that. Two sub-claims are overstated: AndroidTrustManagerVerifier gets indirect device coverage from the BouncyCastle rows of TlsPublicHostTests.cs:59-97 (ExternalNetwork) when run in an Android player, and TrailerFieldValidator is reached by several trailer tests (parser, serializer, HTTP/2 send path), not one. No open issue tracks the decoder or buffer-primitive fixtures.

title: [Testing] Autobahn gate passes when cases are missing, ignores timeouts and failed handshakes, uses an unpinned image and runs only manually
body:
## Summary
check_report.py checks only the cases present in index.json and does not notice a case that did not run unless it is listed in expectations.json. The harness logs timeout and handshake-failed per case but always exits 0, the autobahn-testsuite image has no tag or digest, and the workflow runs only by manual dispatch. A WebSocket conformance regression can therefore pass the gate.

## Location
- `Tools~/autobahn/check_report.py:60`

## Problem
check_report.py:43-58 iterates only over the cases present in index.json and :60-62 adds a problem only for a case listed in expectations.json that did not run; a case that is absent and not listed is not noticed, and the case count the harness prints (Program.cs:46-47) is not compared with len(results). Program.cs:55-63 logs `timeout`/`handshake-failed` per case and always returns 0. run.sh:23 uses `crossbario/autobahn-testsuite` without a tag or digest, unlike the h2-interop images (pinned by digest, #288). autobahn.yml:7-13 has only workflow_dispatch, so a PR that changes Runtime/WebSocket framing or permessage-deflate triggers no conformance run; the fuzz ws targets check exception types, not RFC 6455 behaviour.

**Failure scenario.** On a loaded runner the fuzzing server backs up during group 12, the client's handshakes for 30 later cases time out and the server records nothing for them. The report has 487 entries, all OK, and check_report prints OK. A PR that breaks close-code validation (group 7) merges without any Autobahn run because nobody dispatched the workflow.

## Suggested fix
Have the harness write the case count and its per-case outcomes to a file, and make check_report fail (without --partial) when len(results) differs from the count or any case timed out or failed its handshake without being listed. Pin the image by digest. Add a pull_request trigger on Runtime/WebSocket/** that runs the fast groups (1-7, 10) and keep the long groups for dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The harness writes its case count and per-case outcomes to a file, and check_report fails (without --partial) when the count differs from len(results) or a case timed out or failed its handshake without being listed.
- [ ] The server image is pinned by digest.
- [ ] A pull_request trigger runs the gate on changes under Runtime/WebSocket.
- [ ] Python tests for check_report cover a missing case and a timed-out case.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-22` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.
