title: [Testing] Weekly fuzz run uses a fixed libFuzzer seed and keeps no corpus between runs
body:
## Summary
run.sh passes seed=1 to libFuzzer and fuzz.yml neither overrides it nor caches or uploads the work corpus. Each weekly run starts from the same committed seeds with the same seed and explores the same inputs, so scheduled fuzzing adds no coverage over time.

## Location
- `Tools~/fuzz/run.sh:21`

## Problem
run.sh:21 sets `seed=1` and passes `-seed="$seed"` to libFuzzer (:94); fuzz.yml:92 never passes --seed. New inputs go to .build/fuzz/work/<target> (run.sh:92), which fuzz.yml neither caches nor uploads (the upload step at :94-100 takes only .build/fuzz/artifacts and the log), and the committed corpus is read-only. Tools~/fuzz/corpus holds only seed-* files; no run has added an input.

**Failure scenario.** A parser defect that needs about 5M executions from the seeds to reach is never found: each Monday run executes the same first 1M mutations (budget fuzz.yml:90) and stops. Ten weekly runs give the coverage of one.

## Suggested fix
Persist the work corpus between scheduled runs (actions/cache keyed per target with a restore-key, or an artifact that the next run downloads) and derive the seed from the run number for scheduled runs, keeping seed 1 only for PR runs where reproducibility matters. Print the seed in the log.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scheduled runs derive the seed from the run number and print it in the log; PR runs keep seed 1.
- [ ] The work corpus is persisted between scheduled runs via actions/cache with a restore-key or an uploaded artifact.
- [ ] Two consecutive scheduled runs show the second starting from the first run's corpus.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-15` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Verified: Tools~/fuzz/run.sh:21 `seed=1`, passed as `-seed="$seed"` (:94); fuzz.yml's run step passes only --driver/--target/--runs/--time, never --seed. New inputs go to .build/fuzz/work/<target> (run.sh:92), which fuzz.yml neither caches nor uploads (upload step takes .build/fuzz/artifacts and *.libfuzzer.log only); Tools~/fuzz/corpus holds only seed-* files. Scheduled runs are capped at 1M executions or 3600 s, so each Monday run restarts from the same seeds with the same libFuzzer seed. README documents fixed seeds for the mutate driver (reproducibility) but gives no reason for libFuzzer on schedule. 'Ten runs give the coverage of one' is approximately right; managed-runtime nondeterminism (async scheduling) can make runs diverge a little. Effectiveness gap in a non-required workflow: low.

title: [Testing] A filtered Unity run that matches no test, or a drop in total test count, exits 0
body:
## Summary
summarize_results.py gates only on skipped cases. A filtered run matching zero tests, a fixture that silently disappears or a total that drops reads as a pass, and run-device-tests.sh computes its code from failed == 0. Only the UniTask lane checks for a minimum.

## Location
- `Tools~/unity/summarize_results.py:72`

## Problem
summarize_results.py prints total/passed/failed (:55) and gates only on skipped cases: unexplained skips (:64-69) and, for unfiltered runs, more skips than the baseline (:71-82). run-tests.sh:177-192 exits by Unity's exit code and that gate; run-device-tests.sh:574 computes its code from `failed == "0"`. Nothing fails on total == 0 or on a total below the last known count. Only the UniTask lane has such a gate (run-tests.sh:184-187, exit 4 when no adapter test ran), and testing.md:94 notes that an EditMode run against the runtime assembly discovers 0 tests. CLAUDE.md section 5 makes `run-tests.sh --filter <regex>` the per-change verification.

**Failure scenario.** An agent verifies a fix with `run-tests.sh --platform EditMode --filter Http2FlowControl` (runtime tests are PlayMode) or with a typo in the regex. Unity writes a result file with total=0, the script prints the totals and exits 0, and the PR body says the scoped Unity tests passed. Separately, a fixture compiled out by a new #if on a platform is not a skip, so the Player-Android skip baseline does not notice 40 missing cases.

## Suggested fix
Make summarize_results.py exit 4 when total is 0, and keep a per-target minimum total next to the skip baseline (EditMode, PlayMode, Player-Android) that an unfiltered run must reach; print the delta when the total drops.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] summarize_results.py exits 4 when total is 0.
- [ ] A per-target minimum total (EditMode, PlayMode, Player-Android) is kept next to the skip baseline and an unfiltered run below it fails, printing the delta.
- [ ] Python tests for summarize_results.py cover total 0 and a total below the minimum.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `tests-quality-21` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/tests.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: tests.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Tools~/unity/summarize_results.py:52-83 prints total/passed/failed and returns 4 only for an unexplained skip (:64-69), a missing baseline key or more skips than the baseline on an unfiltered run (:71-82); total is never compared to anything. Tools~/unity/run-tests.sh:172-192 exits 2 only when no result file exists, 1 on a non-zero Unity exit, else the gate code; the only zero-ran check is the UniTask lane (:185-187, unitask_pin.py adapter_cases). run-device-tests.sh derives its code from failed == "0" alone. The comment at run-tests.sh:179-180 says the skip gates exist "so a vanished test cannot pass silently", but a fixture that is deleted or compiled out lowers total and skips together and passes every gate. testing.md:94 itself documents that an EditMode run against the runtime assembly discovers 0 tests, and CLAUDE.md section 5 makes filtered runs the per-change verification. Not re-run here (read-only): that Unity Test Framework 1.1.33 writes a result file with total=0 and exits 0 for a filter that matches nothing is known behaviour and is what the UniTask gate was added for; the missing minimum-total gate for unfiltered runs is settled statically. Mitigation: the script does print total=0. No open issue tracks it (#419, #404 are unrelated).
